title: Interaction surface: tiered legend mode and low-power rendering
creator: Ava Vasquez
description:
Problem: Time-series charts with many series are causing cognitive overload and non-deterministic render costs on low-power devices (battery-optimized laptops, older ARM devices). Current legend behavior renders all series labels and hit targets on initial paint which spikes layout and increases JS main-thread occupancy. Screen reader users also receive noisy ARIA announcements when chart state changes rapidly.

Goal: Design a compact, tiered legend interaction mode that de-prioritizes non-critical series on initial render, surfaces high-priority KPIs first, and shifts secondary series to an overflow / progressive-reveal area. The interaction should reduce initial DOM size and JS computations, use token-driven spacing and color semantics, and provide a predictable, debounced SR announcement strategy for accessibility. Deliverables: component spec, token mapping, motion & microinteraction guidance, keyboard flows, and handoff assets (Figma + acceptance criteria) for engineering implementation and perf validation.
acceptance_criteria: Compact legend mode reduces initial DOM nodes by at least 60% on charts with >20 series (verified by sample dashboard)
Primary KPIs (configurable per chart) are visible and actionable without expansion; secondary series moved to overflow that can be progressively loaded on interaction
Keyboard-only users can traverse primary items, expand the overflow region, and toggle series visibility using standard keyboard patterns (Tab/Enter/Space/Arrow keys)

Screen reader announcements are debounced: only announce initial visible KPIs and a single succinct summary like '12 series; 4 visible, 8 hidden' on chart load; announce individual series toggles when user action occurs
Design tokens defined for compact spacing, condensed font sizes, truncated label rules, and high-contrast focus outlines; tokens included in token catalog with usage notes
Low-power render mode documented: CSS class and recommended JS gating for devices flagged as battery-saver, with a fallback to full mode; guidance for progressive hydration
Figma mockups and interaction prototype delivered, and engineering PR references provided for implementation
Performance regression test (script) demonstrates 30% reduction in main-thread time during initial mount on representative low-power VM
design_notes: Introduce 'tiered' legend concept: primary row (0..N pivots) + overflow chevron that reveals secondary list lazily
Token decisions: use compact-size token group: spacing.s-8, typography.caption, color.gray-600 for muted labels, color.brand-500 for primary KPI accents
Accessibility: use aria-live polite for the initial summary and aria-atomic false for non-essential updates; provide an opt-in verbose aria mode for power-users
Interaction: hover reveals quick-toggle controls; on touch, long-press opens quick actions; persistent keyboard focus ring must match token 'focus.outline-3'
Performance: minimize per-item listeners; delegate events at legend root; render secondary items server-side or via virtualized container when length > 50
Edge cases: stacked series with identical names need disambiguation suffixes; truncated labels should surface full text via accessible tooltip with role='tooltip' and keyboard focusability
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize token mappings and core interaction wireframes; review with accessibility squad
Week 2: engineer prototype for compact legend with event delegation; run perf profile on low-power VM
Week 3: iterate on SR debounce behavior and keyboard flows; integrate with chart runtime caching for progressive reveal
Week 4: QA, cross-browser testing, and merge; add perf regression check to CI
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hiding series by default could confuse existing users — Mitigation: expose a persistent toggle on chart toolbar to switch between 'compact' and 'expanded' legend modes
Risk: ARIA debounce might suppress important change announcements — Mitigation: keep user-initiated toggles immediate and only debounce programmatic/automatic updates
Risk: Increased CSS complexity across tokens causes visual regressions — Mitigation: add visual regression snapshots for legend variants tied to token changes
